record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can measurements of orbital eccentricity e in gravitational-wave signals distinguish primordial binaries formed in the early universe from PBH binaries formed at late times, given that early PBH binaries are expected to circularize before entering current and future detector bands whereas nonzero eccentricity would rule out an early-universe primordial-binary interpretation?

evidence.quote: Even though PBH binaries are formed with large eccentricity at high redshift, they have enough time to circularize before the GW signal can enter the observation band of current and future detectors.

This implies that an observation of a non-zero eccentricity e would rule out the interpretation as a primordial binary formed in the early Universe, while it may still be compatible with a PBH binary formed in the late-time universe [57,58].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a population of binary black hole mergers detected via gravitational waves. Two competing formation scenarios for primordial black hole (PBH) binaries are considered:

(a) Early-universe primordial binaries: pairs of PBHs that decoupled from the cosmological expansion at high redshift (well before matter–radiation equality) and have been inspiralling under gravitational-radiation reaction ever since. Standard analytic and numerical treatments predict that, although such binaries form with very high initial eccentricity (close to 1), the long inspiral time radiates away angular momentum so that, by the time the gravitational-wave signal enters the sensitivity band of present and planned ground- and space-based detectors, the residual eccentricity is effectively zero.

(b) Late-time PBH binaries: binaries assembled at low redshift through dynamical encounters (e.g., gravitational capture in dense PBH halos or clusters), which can retain a measurable nonzero eccentricity when entering the detector band.

Let e denote the orbital eccentricity of a binary inferred from its gravitational-wave signal at a chosen reference frequency in the detector band. Determine whether the measured value of e can be used as a reliable diagnostic to discriminate between scenarios (a) and (b). In particular, address the following:

1. Establish under what assumptions a robust upper bound e_max(scenario a) can be derived such that any measurement e > e_max definitively excludes scenario (a) for a given event.
2. Determine whether a measurement of e consistent with zero, together with other observable parameters of the binary (component masses, spins, redshift), suffices to distinguish PBH binaries of type (a) from astrophysical (stellar-origin) binaries that have also circularized.
3. Quantify the detector sensitivity, waveform-modeling accuracy, and population-level statistics required for such an eccentricity-based discrimination to be operationally feasible.
artifact.category_tag: Gravitational-wave signatures of primordial black hole binaries
artifact.status_search_result: The question of using residual orbital eccentricity to discriminate primordial-black-hole binary formation channels remains an active and open research problem. Recent (2024–2025) reanalyses of LVK events search for eccentricity signatures, with claims of evidence for eccentricity in subpopulations (e.g. GW200208_222617), but no consensus has been reached on whether eccentricity measurements can cleanly separate early-universe PBH binaries (predicted to be circularized) from late-time dynamically formed PBH binaries or astrophysical dynamical channels. Detector sensitivity and waveform-modeling limitations remain bottlenecks.

status_evidence.title: Eccentric or circular? A reanalysis of binary black hole gravitational wave events for orbital eccentricity signatures
status_evidence.snippet: Reanalysis of LVK BBH events searching for eccentricity signatures, indicating ongoing investigation rather than settled resolution.
status_evidence.claim: Discrimination via eccentricity is still under active investigation as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Evidence for eccentricity in the population of binary black holes observed by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
status_evidence.snippet: Population-level study claiming evidence for eccentricity in observed BBHs, relevant to formation-channel discrimination.
status_evidence.claim: Eccentricity-based discrimination of formation channels is an open population-level question.

status_evidence.title: Orbital eccentricities in primordial black hole binaries
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that early-universe PBH binaries circularize before entering detector band, while late-time captures retain eccentricity.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical prediction underlying the proposed diagnostic, but its observational realization remains unresolved.
